title: QTS Data Center
warnings: CONSTRUCTION-PHASE ONLY. This instrument authorizes stormwater discharge from land disturbance and expires 2028-04-22. It states NOTHING about the campus's operating water use, cooling system, process discharge, or electrical load, and it must not be cited for any of them. It does not ground the facility's IT load, which remains the [reference] 500 MW press bracket (see src/watermark/sites/_profiles.py and data/extracted/van-wert/data-centers.md).

The NOI declares Ohio EPA PTI status 'YET_TO_APPLY' and USACE nationwide permit 'YET_TO_APPLY', certified under penalty of law on 2026-07-21. This is the corpus's ONLY instrument-grade statement that no air permit-to-install had been applied for; before it, the absence of a PTI was an unsuccessful-search negative. It dates the negative — it does not promise a future filing, and it says nothing about whether one is required.

Two townships are printed in the NOI's location block (Pleasant AND Ridge, on two County/Township lines) but Ohio EPA's approval letter for the same coverage names Pleasant only. Both are recorded as printed; the discrepancy is not resolved here. Recorded in `facility_address` as the NOI prints it, since the NOI is the applicant's own description of the site.

The NOI carries the FULL facility permit number 2GC08872*AG in its 'Existing NPDES Facility Permit Number' field even though it is the application, submitted 2026-07-21, nine days before the 2026-07-30 approval letter that grants the coverage. Recorded as printed — the same pattern as Sidney's 1GC10596 NOI.
Receiving water is printed as 'Town Creek' with no river mile. The downstream network below is NOT from this document; it is the committed Van Wert hydrology (see stream_network).

The stormwater outlet is Town Creek — the SAME water the City of Van Wert both withdraws its drinking water from and discharges its WWTP effluent to (2PD00006, #1406), which is a finding about the receiving water, not a relationship between the two permits.
